predecessors.name: Golden Horde
predecessors.text: the Lower Volga valley and Volga Delta, the Astrakhan appanage of Mahmud bin Küchük, which broke away from the Great Horde

successors.name: Tsardom of Russia
successors.text: Russia occupied Astrakhan in 1556 and the khanate ended

ledger.x: 1466: Mahmud bin Küchük's Astrakhan Khanate breaks away from the Golden Horde.
1502: Ahmed's line takes the Astrakhan throne as the Great Horde falls.
1523: the Crimean occupation ends within the year.
1549: Crimea occupies Astrakhan again under Sahib I Giray; the page says only that it was 'twice briefly occupied by Crimea' and gives no month.
1549: the second Crimean occupation was brief; the page gives no end date, so the end is entered in the same year as a bridging judgment.
1554: Russia takes Astrakhan town and installs a client khan.
1556: the contest ends in Russian occupation.

wars.name: Russian conquest of Astrakhan
wars.outcome: Russian victory: a client khan installed in 1554, Astrakhan occupied in 1556 and the khanate annexed; the Nogais lost their tribute.

wars.name: Crimean occupations of Astrakhan
wars.outcome: Two brief Crimean occupations, 1523 (under Mehmed I Giray, whose army was destroyed by the Nogais near Astrakhan) and 1549 (under Sahib I Giray); no lasting change of border.

certainty.note: Steppe and river-delta frontiers with the Nogai Horde, the Great Horde and Kazan are approximate; the page describes the land only in words.
